name: Piper PA-42 Cheyenne III/400
summary: Piper's flagship twin turboprop, a stretched Cheyenne with a T-tail and either PT6A or TPE331 engines.

engines: Two turboprops in long slim nacelles
fuselage: Long, narrow, Navajo-derived fuselage with a long pointed nose
Row of small, rounded cabin windows
Door with airstair at the rear left
tail: T-tail with the tailplane on top of the fin

tellTales: T-tail on a low-wing Piper twin turboprop
Long fuselage with a long pointed nose and small rounded windows
Slim turboprop nacelles reaching well ahead of the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The PA-31T Cheyenne I/II is shorter with a low horizontal tail; the PA-42 has a T-tail and a longer fuselage.
The King Air 350 is larger and has bigger, rounded-square windows, a bulkier cabin and often winglets; the PA-42 is slimmer with small round windows.
The King Air F90 also has a T-tail but a shorter, bulkier fuselage with large windows; the PA-42 is longer and slimmer.
